title: Flat Tire
description: The lead truck hits a sharp rock. Hissing air signals another flat.

options.label: Change it yourself (2 hours)
options.outcome: The crew changes the tire in the rain. Back on the road, but behind schedule.

options.label: Use the spare and continue
options.outcome: The spare goes on in ten minutes and holds. You're moving again before the coffee gets cold.
options.failureOutcome: An hour down the same sharp-rock road the spare lets go too. Now there are no spares at all — you crawl the rest of the route in low gear, and tomorrow starts with a tire run to town instead of work.

options.label: Wait for help
options.outcome: Another crew passes by and helps. Cost you half a day.

title: Engine Trouble
description: The crummy coughs and sputters on the climb. Smoke rises from under the hood.

options.label: Field repair with spare parts
options.outcome: Your mechanic chases it to a cracked fuel line and a plugged filter. Fixed by dark, but the spares box is a lot lighter.
options.partialOutcome: It runs, but it should not have to. The fix is a patch on something that lives deeper in the block, and everybody agrees not to say the word rebuild out loud.
options.failureOutcome: It is not a fuel line, it is a spun bearing, and no box of belts fixes that. The truck is dead where it sits — the parts you burned trying are gone, and the tow you were avoiding is now the only call left to make.

options.label: Limp to the next block slowly
options.outcome: Running on half power, you nurse it in. The truck reaches somewhere a proper repair is actually possible.
options.failureOutcome: Halfway there the temperature needle buries itself and the engine seizes with a sound nobody forgets. Now it is a dead truck blocking a bush road, and the tow that was five hundred dollars from camp costs a lot more from here.

options.label: Call for tow truck ($500)
options.outcome: The truck gets hauled out. Expensive, but the right choice.

title: Chainsaw Breakdown
description: The line-clearing saw throws its chain into a stump. Something's bent.

options.label: Swap to backup saw
options.outcome: The backup saw is slower but works. Line clearing drags for the day.

options.label: Send runner for parts
options.outcome: Someone burns the afternoon driving to town. The dealer has the bar and chain in stock, and the good saw runs again by morning.
options.failureOutcome: The runner comes back at dusk with a chocolate bar and no parts — the dealer stopped stocking that bar two seasons ago. It is the slow backup saw until a proper order comes up from Kamloops, and line cutting is capped until it does.

options.label: Try to straighten the bar
options.outcome: With a vise block, a straightedge, and patience, the bar comes back true enough to cut. It will finish the season if nobody pinches it again.
options.failureOutcome: The third hammer blow finds the stress point and the bar cracks clean through the rail. The good saw is a paperweight until a new bar arrives, and the backup becomes the whole show.

title: Truck Stuck in Mud
description: The truck sinks to its axles in soft ground. It's not going anywhere without help.

options.label: Winch it off a stump with the truck's own winch
options.outcome: The winch line goes around a big stump and does the rest, slow and ugly. The truck comes free with the fenders full of muskeg.
options.failureOutcome: The stump you anchored to is rotten through — it lets go on the second pull and the truck settles deeper. Now the winch line is buried with it and nothing left in camp is big enough to pull it out. It is shovels and brush now, or waiting on drier weather.

options.label: Dig and lay brush road
options.outcome: Everyone grabs shovels. Exhausting work but it works.

options.label: Leave it and walk out
options.outcome: You hike back with essential gear. The truck waits for drier weather.

title: Sudden Storm
description: Dark clouds roll in fast. Lightning flashes over the ridge.

options.label: Take shelter immediately
options.outcome: Everyone piles into vehicles. Safe but no work gets done.

options.label: Push through to the next block
options.outcome: You beat the worst of it over the ridge with lightning walking the far side of the valley. Nobody says it was a good idea, but it worked.
options.failureOutcome: A snag lets go across the road with the trucks strung out over a kilometre and no way to turn around. One man takes a limb across the shoulder clearing it, and you end up sheltering anyway — in the open, in the worst of it, in the worst possible spot.

options.label: Set up emergency camp
options.outcome: Tarps go up fast. You wait out the worst. Morale holds.

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: The creek you crossed this morning is now a torrent. Water's rising fast.

options.label: Move to high ground immediately
options.outcome: Everyone scrambles uphill. Equipment is safe but the day is lost.

options.label: Risk crossing now before it gets worse
options.outcome: The trucks take it in convoy with the water shoving at the doors. Everyone makes the far bank, engines screaming, hearts going.
options.partialOutcome: The second truck loses the line mid-channel and hangs up on the downstream boulders. The winch gets it to the far bank before the water wins, but everything in the box rode the creek to get there.
options.failureOutcome: The lead truck loses its footing and slews sideways into the current, taking water over the hood before anyone can react. You drag everybody out on a rope and watch it settle. You are still on the wrong side, minus one engine, and the water is still coming up.

options.label: Camp on this side overnight
options.outcome: You wait for waters to drop. Lost a day but everyone's dry.

title: Extreme Cold Snap
description: Temperature drops to -30C overnight. Everything is frozen solid.

options.label: Keep vehicles running all night
options.outcome: Engines stay warm but fuel tanks drain fast.

options.label: Bundle up and wait it out
options.outcome: Everyone doubles up in the warmest tents and nobody does anything heroic. A few white patches on cheeks, but it stays at scares.
options.failureOutcome: By morning the compassman can't feel two fingers, and by noon they're the wrong colour. He's bandaged, off the line, and you're short a set of hands with the cold snap still parked overhead.

options.label: Light a big warming fire
options.outcome: The fire keeps spirits high. Extra food consumed for energy.

title: Bear in Camp
description: A black bear has found the food cache. It's not happy about being interrupted.

options.label: Make noise and back away slowly
options.outcome: Pots, air horns, and slow steps backward. The bear takes one more mouthful on principle and ambles into the bush. Some food is ruined.
options.failureOutcome: The noise means nothing to a bear that has already found the calories. She works the cache methodically while you stand there banging pots, and what she doesn't eat she ruins. Worse, she's learned exactly where dinner lives — this camp has a bear problem now.

options.label: Use bear spray
options.outcome: Direct hit at eight metres. The bear leaves at speed. Everyone's shaken but safe.
options.failureOutcome: The wind swings just as the can goes off and the cloud comes back over your own people. Two of them spend the day blind and retching in the creek while the bear, unbothered, finishes what's left of the cache.

options.label: Bang pots, then strip the camp of attractants and move the food to the truck
options.outcome: The noise buys you the minutes you need. Every cooler, grease can and garbage bag goes into the locked truck and the cook tent gets scrubbed. She circles once at dusk, finds nothing, and moves on.

options.label: Report the habituated bear (RAPP line)
options.outcome: You call it in to the RAPP line from the ridge where the phone reaches. The conservation officer logs it, asks about attractants, and tells you what you already know: fix the camp before she comes back.

title: Grizzly Territory
description: Fresh grizzly signs everywhere. Tracks, scat, claw marks on trees. This is her home.

options.label: Post bear watch and continue
options.outcome: The watch stands on the high stump with the air horn and the day goes by in nervous glances. She never shows. Productivity suffers anyway.
options.failureOutcome: Mid-afternoon the watch's horn goes and she is there, close, ears back. The pull-out is fast and ugly — tools left where they dropped. Nobody goes back into that block without a new plan and a second look at the sign, and the crew has made it clear they're in no hurry.

options.label: Relocate operations for the day
options.outcome: You move to a different area. Safe but inefficient.

options.label: Bear-aware protocol: pairs, spray, hourly radio checks
options.outcome: Nobody runs line alone. Every pair carries spray on the hip, not in the pack, and the radio check goes out on the hour. Slower, noisier, and everyone sleeps.

title: Moose on the Road
description: A bull moose stands in the middle of the road. He's not moving.

options.label: Wait him out
options.outcome: After 20 minutes of staring, he finally ambles off.

options.label: Honk and creep forward
options.outcome: He charges, bounces off the bull bar, and stomps into the willows to think about it. Minor dents; everyone's okay.
options.failureOutcome: He rears up and puts both hooves through the grille. Coolant sprays across the road and the gauge climbs before you've backed off fifty metres. The truck is done moving until the radiator is, and he stands over his victory for another half hour.

options.label: Find an alternate route
options.outcome: A longer path but no wildlife confrontation.

title: Caribou Herd Crossing
description: A herd of caribou is crossing ahead. Dozens of them, taking their time.

options.label: Stop and watch respectfully
options.outcome: Beautiful sight. The crew takes photos. Good for morale.

options.label: Radio ahead about the delay
options.outcome: Office appreciates the update. Lost an hour.

options.label: Try to pass slowly
options.outcome: You idle through the gaps and the herd flows around the truck. Saved an hour; nobody feels great about it.
options.failureOutcome: The herd breaks the wrong way and pours down the ditch line in a panic — right past a conservation officer's parked truck at the junction. Southern mountain caribou are listed under SARA and he was writing before you'd stopped. The complaint lands with C&E with your plate number on it.

title: Worker Injury
description: A crew member slips on a wet log along the traverse and goes down hard, clutching their ankle.

options.label: Have the OFA 3 tape it and keep them on light duty
options.outcome: Taped, laced tight, back on light duty. Sore for days, but it's a sprain and it behaves like one.
options.failureOutcome: By supper the ankle is the size of a grapefruit and the wrong colour, and they can't put any weight on it. It was never a sprain. The ETV goes out at first light, the X-ray says fracture, and the OFA 3 does the math on your call. They're off the crew for the season.

options.label: Send them out for medical care in the ETV
options.outcome: The ETV heads to town with the OFA 3 riding along. You're short-handed but it's the right call.

options.label: Have them rest in camp
options.outcome: Two days of camp rest, elevation, and cold creek water. By the second morning they're walking it off.
options.failureOutcome: Overnight it balloons until the boot won't go on. You send them out in the ETV in the morning anyway — a day later than you should have, and the X-ray will say exactly that. They're off the crew for the season.

title: Bad Food
description: Half the crew woke up sick. Something in last night's dinner didn't agree.

options.label: Rest day for the sick
options.outcome: Those affected stay in camp. Work continues short-handed.

options.label: Push through anyway
options.outcome: Everyone works, sort of. Production limps, tempers are short, and the outhouse sees heavy traffic — but the day ends with everyone upright.
options.failureOutcome: Mid-morning one of the sick ones goes down on a bluff along the traverse line and cracks his head on a rock. He's concussed where he landed. Work stops, and the near-miss write-up asks in plain language why sick people were on a steep line.

options.label: Dispose of suspect food
options.outcome: You throw out everything questionable. Food stores depleted.

title: Chainsaw Accident

managerVariant.title: Serious Injury - Medevac Decision
managerVariant.description: A layout tech took a kickback to the leg clearing line on the north block. The OFA 3 has the bleeding controlled, barely. The superintendent needs an answer while the helicopter company holds the line.

options.label: Authorize the medevac charter
options.outcome: The helicopter is airborne in twenty minutes. The invoice is a number; the alternative wasn't.

options.label: Send him out by road with the first aid attendant
options.outcome: Three hours of logging road with a compression bandage. He makes it. The division logs every kilometre.

options.label: Tell them to stabilize on site and finish the shift
options.outcome: Production holds. So does the story, which is already moving from camp to camp - and WorkSafeBC takes calls from anyone.

description: A saw kicks back clearing line. There's blood. This is serious.

options.label: Call helicopter medevac
options.outcome: The OFA 3 has the bleed controlled and the air ambulance is on the ground within the hour. The bill is steep, but the crew sees that people come before the line.

options.label: First aid, then the ETV to hospital with the OFA 3 aboard
options.outcome: Pressure bandage, elevation, and three hours of washboard road with the OFA 3 in the back of the ETV. The bleeding stays controlled the whole way and the ER takes it from there.
options.failureOutcome: An hour out the bandage soaks through and he goes grey and quiet. The OFA 3 keeps him talking. The ER stabilizes him, but the damage done on that road is the kind that ends seasons. Everyone in camp knows a helicopter would have had him there in forty minutes, and the incident review will ask why it wasn't called.

options.label: Treat on site and keep the crew working
options.outcome: The bandage holds and he rides out the day in the crummy, white-faced. It was the cheap choice and everyone knows it, but it didn't get worse.
options.partialOutcome: By the third day the wound is hot, swollen, and weeping through the dressing. You send him to town on the supply run — a planned evacuation instead of an emergency, which is the most that can be said for it. You lost the worker anyway.
options.failureOutcome: Three days on, the leg is septic and he's running a fever of thirty-nine and change in a camp four hours from pavement. The helicopter you didn't call the first time comes anyway, on worse terms, with worse odds. WorkSafeBC opens a file on why a severe laceration was treated with a bandage and a shift schedule.

title: Road Washed Out

managerVariant.title: Mainline Washout
managerVariant.description: The mainline went into the creek overnight and nothing is moving in or out. The road contractor wants direction before he mobilizes, and the division wants it in writing.

options.label: Authorize an emergency bypass
options.outcome: The contractor punches a rough detour through in two days. It's ugly, it's over budget, and it moves wood.

options.label: Stand the division down for the engineered repair
options.outcome: A proper fix, a proper delay. The quarter absorbs it; the safety file appreciates it.

options.label: Let them push loads through the low-water crossing
options.outcome: It works until it doesn't. Equipment takes a beating, and everyone downstream develops an opinion.

description: The road ahead has collapsed into the creek. No way through.

options.label: Build a bypass
options.outcome: With shovels and chainsaws, you cut a rough detour. Takes all day.

options.label: Report and wait for road crew
options.outcome: You spend the shift on the radio with the office and the road permit holder, then waiting on a temporary crossing. The road reopens by closeout, with slow travel through the repair next shift.

options.label: Try to ford the creek
options.outcome: You pick the widest, shallowest braid and take it slow. The truck grinds over the cobble, scrapes bottom twice, and climbs the far bank streaming water.
options.partialOutcome: Mid-channel the front end drops into a slot between boulders and hangs there, driveline grinding. Winching it the rest of the way takes two hours, and the undercarriage keeps some parts of the creek as souvenirs.
options.failureOutcome: The bed of the ford is washout spoil, not creek bottom, and it swallows the front wheel whole. Water comes over the intake before the winch line is even hooked. The engine is drowned, the washout is still there, and you are building the bypass anyway — now with one less truck to do it.

title: Questionable Bridge
description: The log-stringer bridge ahead looks... tired. Nobody is sure it will hold the truck.

options.label: Check the bridge tag and the road permit holder's last inspection
options.outcome: The tag is on the abutment post and the office pulls the RP holder's inspection sheet: rated for light vehicles, last looked at in the spring. You cross at a walk, one truck at a time, and note the sag for the next report.

options.label: Walk it and look at the stringers and abutments, then cross empty, one truck
options.outcome: You walk it, bouncing on the stringers at the mid-span, and get a light down under the abutments. It talks back but it does not move. Trucks go one at a time, empty, very slowly, and everyone watches.
options.partialOutcome: Underfoot it is fine. Under a loaded crummy it is not — a stringer splits on the first truck and the deck sags ten centimetres. You get across. Nothing is coming back this way.
options.failureOutcome: It holds you and lets go under the truck. The rear duals drop through the deck onto the cribbing and stop there, which is the only luck in it. The rest of the day is spent getting the truck out, and the crossing is finished.

options.label: Find another crossing
options.outcome: A longer route around. Burns fuel but no bridge worries.

title: Landslide Debris
description: A slope has let go across the road. Trees, mud, and rock block the path.

options.label: Winch the stems off with the truck and shovel the rest
options.outcome: The truck winches stems off one at a time while everyone else watches the slope above. By late afternoon there's a lane.
options.failureOutcome: Nobody hears the second pulse over the winch — the first anyone knows is mud coming down across the hood. The driver bails out the far side unhurt; the truck stays, buried to the doors. Now you make the call to the geotech you were trying to avoid, and add a vehicle recovery to the file.

options.label: Hand-clear a path
options.outcome: Everyone grabs a saw or a shovel. It's brutal work, but by dark there's a path wide enough for the trucks.
options.failureOutcome: The slope gives a second time with six people in the cut. Everyone comes out, limping and swearing, but two shovels and a saw are somewhere under the new material. Nobody argues about the next step anymore — you pull back, and the road stays closed until someone qualified says otherwise.

options.label: Turn back and report
options.outcome: Safety first. The office will get a qualified geotech to look at it before anyone drives through.

title: Passing Supply Truck
description: Another crew's supply truck is passing through. They've got extras.

options.label: Trade for fuel
options.outcome: You swap some food for fuel. Fair trade.

options.label: Trade for food
options.outcome: Fresh supplies for the camp. Morale rises.

options.label: Just share news
options.outcome: Good conversation and road updates. Nothing more.

title: Supplies Lost
description: A load shifted on the rough road. A box of supplies bounced off somewhere.

options.label: Go back and search
options.outcome: Twenty minutes back down the road, there it is — burst open in the ditch but mostly salvageable. Lost time and fuel, nothing worse.
options.failureOutcome: You find where it went over — a rock bluff the road bends around. The box is forty metres down, burst, contents strewn through the alder and soaked. You drive back with the fuel burned, the hours gone, and the write-off intact, and the shortfall moves the next resupply run up a week.

options.label: Write it off and continue
options.outcome: Can't spare the time. The lost supplies go on the books.

options.label: Secure remaining cargo
options.outcome: You stop to re-tie everything. No more losses.

title: Excellent Road Conditions
description: The road ahead is in great shape - recently graded and smooth.

options.label: Make up time!
options.outcome: The crew pushes forward quickly on the good road. Great progress!

options.label: Take it easy, save fuel
options.outcome: You cruise at low RPMs. Fuel gauge barely moves.

title: Abandoned Supply Cache
description: You spot an old camp with some leftover supplies. Looks usable.

options.label: Scavenge fuel and parts
options.outcome: A few jerry cans of diesel that smell right, and a box of belts in the right sizes. The bush provides.
options.failureOutcome: The cans sat through too many freeze-thaws and nobody checked with a clear jar. By mid-morning the truck's filters are plugged with rust and water, and it is down while somebody drains and bleeds the whole system. The free fuel cost more than town prices.

options.label: Grab the food supplies
options.outcome: Canned goods and dried rations, labels faded but seals intact. Still good.
options.failureOutcome: Dinner tastes fine. Breakfast doesn't happen — half the camp is at the outhouse or in their bags, and the tins get a proper look in daylight: bulged lids, rust through the seams. The haul goes in a pit, and the day runs short-handed.

options.label: Take the first aid kit
options.outcome: A dusty but complete first aid kit. Could be a lifesaver.

title: Beautiful Sunset
description: The evening sky puts on a spectacular show. Everyone stops to watch.

options.label: Knock off early and watch it from the ridge
options.outcome: Twenty minutes of line left undone. Moments like this remind everyone why they love this work.

options.label: Keep working but appreciate it
options.outcome: Even while busy, the beauty lifts spirits.

title: Helpful Locals
description: Two members of the Nation on their way to fish camp stop at the truck with advice and coffee.

options.label: Share a meal and listen
options.outcome: They point out a shortcut, warn about a washout ahead, and tell you which crossing the map lies about.

options.label: Trade for supplies
options.outcome: They have smoked salmon to trade. Delicious and nutritious!

title: Equipment Running Smoothly
description: Everything is humming along perfectly today. Not a single mechanical issue.

options.label: Keep up the momentum
options.outcome: A productive day with no breakdowns. Equipment looks even better.

options.label: Do preventive maintenance
options.outcome: With things running well, you take time to check everything over.

title: Peat Crossing Starts Pumping
description: A probe rod drops through the road edge and brown water wells up. The peat mat under the approach is losing strength faster than the road card suggested.

options.label: Flag the soft ground and back crews off
options.outcome: You mark the weak spots, limit traffic, and keep the problem from becoming a full blowout.

options.label: Lay brush and corduroy the approach
options.outcome: The crew spends the shift laying brush and corduroy. The mat takes the weight and spreads it — the crossing holds, and everyone feels the day in their backs.
options.failureOutcome: The mat under the corduroy is worse than the probe said. Under the first loaded pass the whole approach pumps, floats, and blows out sideways — the truck backs off a crossing that no longer exists. The shift is spent, the crossing is closed, and from tomorrow everything goes the long way.

options.label: Test it with one light pickup
options.outcome: The pickup idles across with a man walking ahead reading the mat. It flexes, it weeps a little brown water, and it holds. Light traffic only, but the crossing is a crossing.
options.partialOutcome: The pickup squeaks through, but its wake follows it — the shoulders slump and brown water stands in the ruts by evening. It's a light-vehicle crossing now, and only just.
options.failureOutcome: Ten metres out the mat quits. The front end drops through to the frame and brown water comes up over the running boards. Recovering a truck off pumping peat takes the day, wrecks what was left of the approach, and settles the question — this crossing is done, and the block reroutes around it.

title: Fish Passage Red Flag
description: The crossing looks rougher on the ground than on the map: fresh scour, perched flow, and salmon visible below the pipe but not above it.

options.label: Close the crossing to the crew's trucks and call it in
options.outcome: You stop the trucks, document the outlet, and get it into the engineering queue before more damage is done.

options.label: Photograph the outlet, GPS it, red-flag the crossing for the engineer's fish-passage assessment
options.outcome: Photos of the perched outlet with a tape in frame, a GPS point, and a red-flag note on the road card. The engineer has what she needs for the fish-passage assessment, and the office knows about it before anyone else does.

options.label: Keep moving and note it for later
options.outcome: The pipe holds one more day and you bank the traverse. The note goes in the field book for later, where it sits with all the other laters.
options.partialOutcome: The crossing holds. What you didn't see was the hatchery crew downstream, and the photos of the perched outlet — with your crummy on top — are on a district desk by Friday. Nobody calls. A file just opens.
options.failureOutcome: Mid-afternoon the culvert lets go completely. The road drops a metre, the truck barely stops in time, and a brown plume rolls through the pool where the spawners were holding. This one isn't a note for later — it's a DFO file, and the crossing is gone.

title: Smoke Hold at Camp
description: Smoke settles over camp and the air quality keeps climbing. The block is still there, but the work window is shrinking by the hour.

options.label: Stand crews down and switch to low-exposure tasks
options.outcome: You burn the shift on mapping, maintenance, and reporting until the air improves.

options.label: Run a shortened shift with respirators
options.outcome: Some work gets done, but nobody mistakes it for a normal day.

options.label: Push a full shift anyway
options.outcome: The numbers look better by supper. The crew is hoarse and drained, and the call gets harder to defend every hour, but it holds.
options.failureOutcome: Mid-afternoon the compassman goes down on the hill, hands on knees and then all the way down, coughing like a man twice his age. The stand-down order comes over the radio while you're still getting him to the truck. You shut down anyway — later, with an injury on the books and nothing to show for the difference.

title: Patchy Regen Stress
description: A beetle-era planting block looks fine from the road, but the walk-through tells a different story: thin stocking on hot knolls, brush pressure in the draws, and seedlings already losing ground.

options.label: Re-stratify the block and hit the worst patches first
options.outcome: You focus effort where survival is slipping fastest and get ahead of the worst failures.

options.label: Order fill-plant and brush follow-up
options.outcome: The prescription gets more expensive, but the stand has a better chance of evening out.

options.label: Leave it for the formal survey window
options.outcome: You save today's budget and lose time while the weak patches keep declaring themselves.

title: Discovery of the Ancient Grove
description: Running the east boundary, the crew walks into a grove of cedar that nobody's inventory shows: veterans well over two metres at breast height, some of them older than the treaty. It is inside the block as drawn.

options.label: Flag it for the OGMA / big-tree screening and call the district
options.outcome: You GPS the biggest stems, tape the diameters, and ribbon a reserve around the grove. The planner takes it into the OGMA screening and the district's stewardship forester wants to walk it. The boundary moves.

options.label: Leave it out of the package — ribbon the boundary straight through it and don't mention the diameters
options.outcome: The line goes through the grove without a plot card. The block keeps its volume, the package goes in clean, and the diameters stay in your field book. Word travels anyway — the cruiser saw the tape too.

title: Crew Member Threatens to Quit
description: Your most experienced layout tech corners you after dinner. He says he's had enough — the pay isn't worth the conditions. He wants out tomorrow morning.

options.label: Let them go
options.outcome: He packs up at dawn. The crew watches in silence. You're short-handed now.

options.label: Negotiate — offer a bonus and lighter duties
options.outcome: He thinks about it for a long minute and puts his gloves back on. Word gets around camp that you sorted it out instead of letting him walk.
options.failureOutcome: He takes the money, works two more days, and is gone with the Thursday supply run. You are down a set of hands and out the bonus.
options.partialOutcome: He stays, and he is careful to let everyone know exactly what it took. By supper two others have found reasons to mention how tired they are.

options.label: Ignore it — he'll cool off
options.outcome: By morning his gloves are on and nothing more is said. But the crew noticed you didn't care enough to ask, and the tension doesn't leave with the mood.
options.failureOutcome: His bunk is empty at dawn and his truck is gone through the gate. The crew ate breakfast watching you not notice, and now they're doing his work short-handed for a boss who shrugged.

title: Unauthorized Logging Nearby
description: You find fresh-cut stumps and skid trails on the adjacent block. Someone's been logging here without a cutting permit or a timber mark — and it's not anyone you know.

options.label: Call it in — RAPP line and the district's natural resource officer
options.outcome: You call the RAPP line from the ridge where the phone reaches and the office follows up with the district's NRO. Someone will want your photos and the GPS points; nobody needs your day.

options.label: Ignore it — not your problem
options.outcome: You keep working. The stumps grey out, the tire tracks wash away, and nobody ever asks what you saw.
options.failureOutcome: Six weeks later a natural resource officer walks your block with photos of the stumps and your crew's tire tracks beside them. You work two hundred metres from a theft site and saw nothing — that goes in the file, worded exactly that way, and the file follows you for the rest of the season.

options.label: Investigate quietly on your own
options.outcome: You go in on foot after dark and get what you came for — plate numbers, a photo of the machine's serial plate, the gate coordinates. Nobody sees you. Whatever happens next, you have proof.
options.failureOutcome: Headlights swing across the clearing while you're still beside their machine, and you leave through the slash at a dead run. No photos, no plates — but they got a good look at you. When the visit comes, it'll be them holding the cards.

title: Confrontation at the Cutblock
description: A battered pickup rolls up to your camp. Two rough-looking guys step out — they know you've been snooping around their operation.

options.label: Stand your ground and tell them to leave
options.outcome: You meet them in the middle of camp with the whole crew drifting in behind you. There's a lot of talk, none of it kind, and then they leave. They don't come back.
options.failureOutcome: They leave without a word, which should have been the warning. In the morning three tires are flat with clean knife cuts and the fuel tank's water trap is full of something that isn't diesel. The trucks stay parked while you sort it out, and you call the NRO you could have called yesterday — now as the victim, not the witness.

options.label: Offer to look the other way
options.outcome: They nod, and that's the whole transaction. Their operation and yours ignore each other for the rest of the season, and nobody ever asks you what you knew.
options.failureOutcome: Months later a C&E investigation rolls up their operation, and they hand over your name before the coffee's poured — the licensee next door who agreed to look away. Every inspection you get for the rest of the season starts from that sentence.

options.label: Call the NRO and the RCMP immediately
options.outcome: The district's natural resource officer and an RCMP member arrive within hours. The pickup is gone before they get there. You did the right thing.

title: Discounted Flight Time
description: A local pilot's afternoon charter was cancelled. At a reduced rate, the pilot can sling supplies to your next block or fly an aerial reconnaissance.

options.label: Sling supplies ahead ($2,000)
options.outcome: Two thousand dollars of flight time and the fuel and gear are waiting at the next block. Massive time savings.

options.label: Aerial recon of the route ($1,800)
options.outcome: An hour in the front seat, eighteen hundred dollars on the card. From above you spot a washout, a good crossing, and the best line for the traverse.

options.label: Save the money for emergencies
options.outcome: You wave him off. The budget stays intact but you wonder what could have been.

title: A Key Crew Member Is Sick
description: One of your strongest crew members is feverish, pale, and clearly struggling. They insist they can keep working.

options.label: Send them back to rest in camp
options.outcome: They sleep through the shift. You lose a strong producer today, but rest gives them the best chance to recover by tomorrow.

options.label: Let them do light duty
options.outcome: They sort the ribbon box and file the saw chain by the fire, moving slow but staying warm. Not much use today, but they hold steady and are up and moving by morning.
options.failureOutcome: By mid-afternoon they are flat on their back in the cook tent, and by dark two more are running fevers. The flu is in camp now, and light duty is what everyone will be doing for a while.

options.label: Medicate and push through
options.outcome: Ibuprofen and cold pills out of the kit. They work at half speed, say nothing at lunch, and make it to the whistle without going down.
options.failureOutcome: An hour after lunch they go down between the rows, soaked through and shaking hard. This is not a flu you walk off, and the conversation now is about the drive to town, not tomorrow's shift.

title: WorkSafeBC Site Visits This Week
description: Word from the office: a WorkSafeBC prevention officer is doing site visits in the district this week. Better get things in order.

options.label: Spend the day prepping for inspection
options.outcome: You clean up the site, check PPE and the ETV, and get the ERP, the tailgate records and the check-in log in order. Lost a day on the line but you'll be ready.

options.label: Do a quick tidy and keep working
options.outcome: A half-hearted cleanup. Things look okay-ish. You keep the line moving.

options.label: Ignore it — we're always compliant
options.outcome: You trust your standards. The crew keeps working at full pace.

title: WorkSafeBC Officer Arrives
description: A WorkSafeBC truck pulls into camp. The prevention officer steps out with a tablet and asks for the crew lead, the OFA 3, and the emergency response plan.

options.label: Give them the full tour confidently
options.outcome: You walk her through the ERP, the ETV, the check-in procedure and the tailgate records, and it takes most of the day. She notes a few minor items but leaves satisfied.

options.label: Be cooperative but let them lead
options.outcome: You answer what she asks and nothing more. She finds a frayed lanyard and a dated extinguisher, notes both without drama, and is gone by two.
options.failureOutcome: She finds the thing you did not know about — the ETV's stretcher straps rotted through and last year's repeater channel in the ERP. An order goes on the crew until both are fixed and signed off, and a follow-up visit lands on the calendar.

options.label: Distract them with coffee and stories
options.outcome: She takes the coffee, tells a better story than yours, and gives the site a light once-over between refills. The crew never stops working.
options.failureOutcome: She sets the cup down half-finished and starts opening the first aid kit. By the end of it you have orders on three items, a lecture about wasting her time, and your operation flagged for an unannounced re-visit.

title: Suspicious Tracks Near Camp
description: Large canine tracks circle the camp perimeter. Too big for coyote. The food scraps from last night are gone.

options.label: Set up better food storage and carry on
options.outcome: You hang food higher and secure the garbage. Probably just a lone wolf passing through.

options.label: Post a night watch
options.outcome: Someone stays up with a flashlight. Tired crew tomorrow.

options.label: Call it in to the RAPP line
options.outcome: The conservation officer logs it and tells you to be cautious. Standard advice.

title: Wolf Pack Sighting
description: At dusk, five grey wolves emerge from the treeline and watch your camp from the ridge. They're not afraid.

options.label: Light extra fires and make noise
options.outcome: The wolves linger on the ridge but keep their distance. An uneasy night of banging pots and feeding fires. They are gone by morning.
options.failureOutcome: The noise holds their eyes on the ridge while two of them work the cache behind camp. By morning half the meat is gone and the crew has done the math — until the pack moves on, nobody works spread out.

options.label: Move camp to a more open area
options.outcome: A pain to relocate but worth it. No more wolf visits.

options.label: Carry on — wolves don't attack people
options.outcome: You're right, mostly. They shadow the camp for two days and lose interest. The crew doesn't sleep well the whole time.
options.failureOutcome: A wolf takes a cooler off the tailgate at noon, six metres from the cruiser. Habituated is the word the conservation officer uses. Nobody works alone after that and nobody works at dusk, and the pace shows it.

title: Radio Report: Incoming Weather System
description: The weather service broadcasts a warning: a major system is building to the west. Heavy rain and wind expected within 48 hours.

options.label: Push hard now to get ahead of it
options.outcome: The crew works double-time and hates it. But the traverse is ahead of schedule when the first gusts arrive, and that is money in the bank.
options.failureOutcome: Double-time is when corners get cut. The crummy drops a wheel off a soft shoulder on a spur it had no business on, and it is still sitting there when the front rolls in. You meet the storm tired, behind, and down a truck.

options.label: Prepare camp for the storm
options.outcome: You batten down the hatches. Tarps, drainage ditches, extra firewood. Ready as you'll ever be.

options.label: Fall back to a safer position
options.outcome: You retreat to lower ground near the main road. Safe but far from the work site.

title: Major Storm Hits
description: The storm arrives with a vengeance. Trees bend sideways, rain comes in sheets, and the road turns to soup. No one's working today.

options.label: Hunker down and ride it out
options.outcome: A long, wet, miserable day of cards and coffee while the tarps snap. But everything holds together. Barely.
options.failureOutcome: Around midnight a cottonwood lets go and comes down across the frame tent — nobody under it, which is the only luck going. The generator and a wall tent are wrecked, and the first dry day goes to rebuilding camp instead of working.

options.label: Evacuate to the main road
options.outcome: A white-knuckle drive with the wipers losing. Everyone makes it to the main road, and camp is on its own until this blows through.
options.failureOutcome: The crummy slides off the shoulder where the ditch has taken the road, halfway between camp and the highway. You spend the night in the cabs listening to it blow, and tomorrow belongs to the recovery, not the job.

options.label: Use the downtime for equipment maintenance
options.outcome: Can't go anywhere, might as well wrench. Surprisingly productive shelter time.

title: Old-Growth Cedar Grove
description: Pushing through dense brush, you stumble into a cathedral-like grove of ancient cedars. Some of these trees are 500 years old. Sunlight filters through the canopy like stained glass.

options.label: Flag it for the big-tree / OGMA screening and call the office
options.outcome: The planner pulls it into the OGMA screening and the boundary moves. Your compliance record shines.

options.label: GPS it for yourself and keep the diameters out of the notes
options.outcome: You GPS the location for your own records and leave the diameters out of the plot cards. A private treasure — and a gap in the package if anyone ever walks it.

options.label: Let the crew take a break here
options.outcome: Everyone sits among the giants in awed silence. Someone says it's the best moment of the season.

title: Unmapped Creek Crossing
description: Your traverse crosses a creek that doesn't appear on any map. It's not huge, but it's definitely fish-bearing — you can see spawning beds.

options.label: Classify it — width, gradient, fish presence — and put the RMA on the map
options.outcome: Channel width, gradient, a look for fish and the default riparian class: S4, thirty-metre RMA. Two hours with the stream card and the camera, and the boundary moves before anyone has to ask.

options.label: Call it S6 from the truck
options.outcome: You write S6 in the field book from the cab, ford the wide cobble bar, and keep moving. Should have walked it, and you know it, but the day keeps moving.
options.failureOutcome: The bank cuts loose under the second truck and a plume of silt runs a hundred metres down through the spawning beds. A creek that is not on your map is on somebody's — a natural resource officer is out within the week with photographs, and DFO gets a copy. It is a fisheries file now, with your name in it.

options.label: Flag it and reroute the traverse; let the planner classify it
options.outcome: You ribbon a wide detour and hand it to the office as unclassified. The planner will send someone back with a stream card — the file waits for that.

title: Historical Survey Markers
description: Rusted iron pins and blazed trees — someone surveyed this area decades ago. The old markers could help confirm your boundary lines.

options.label: Record and photograph everything
options.outcome: Detailed documentation of the old survey. This data is gold for boundary disputes.

options.label: Use them to verify your current lines
options.outcome: Cross-referencing reveals your map is off by 40 metres. Good catch before the boundary goes in wrong.

options.label: Note the location and keep moving
options.outcome: You GPS the pins and carry on. Useful info but not explored fully.

title: Abandoned Trapper's Cabin
description: Hidden in a stand of spruce, you find a weathered log cabin. The roof is mostly intact. Inside: a rusty stove, some old traps, and shelves of dusty supplies.

options.label: Use it as an emergency shelter
options.outcome: You patch the roof and clear it out. A solid backup shelter if weather turns nasty.

options.label: Salvage the supplies
options.outcome: Kerosene, rope, a hand axe, and canned goods that are somehow still sealed. The cook inspects every tin and keeps most of them. Lucky find.
options.failureOutcome: Sealed is not the same as sound. By three in the morning half the camp is outside the tents being sick, the cook worst of all. First aid gets everyone through it; the next day of production does not happen.

options.label: Leave it — it's on someone's trapline
options.outcome: You photograph it, GPS it, and leave it. The office runs it past the trapline holder and the archaeology screening; both appreciate the call.

title: High-Stakes Card Game
description: Tensions have been simmering. After dinner, a poker game gets heated. Two crew members are about to come to blows over a $200 pot.

options.label: Break it up and ban gambling
options.outcome: Order is restored but everyone resents the fun police. Quiet, sullen camp.

options.label: Mediate — split the pot and move on
options.outcome: A fair-enough solution. Nobody's happy but nobody's fighting, and by breakfast it is mostly a story.
options.failureOutcome: The man who was winning takes the split as robbery with a referee. He does not swing, he just stops talking — and now they work opposite ends of the block, and you plan every day around keeping them there.

options.label: Let them sort it out themselves
options.outcome: They scuffle behind the fuel shed. One gets a black eye, the pot gets settled, and somehow they respect each other more after.
options.partialOutcome: Nobody swings. The winner pockets the pot, the loser goes to his tent, and the thing sits there festering. They will not run line together now, and you are building each day's plan around it.
options.failureOutcome: It goes to the ground and somebody's hand finds a stump. Broken, splinted, done working — and by morning the loser is asking to be on the next supply run out. You are down a working pair of hands either way.

title: Radio Goes Dead
description: The camp radio crackles and dies mid-transmission. No signal, no spare parts. You're cut off from the outside.

options.label: Send someone to town for a replacement
options.outcome: A full day's drive, round trip. You're without comms until they return.

options.label: Try to fix it with what you have
options.outcome: A cracked solder joint on the power board. Your handiest tech reflows it with a screwdriver blade heated on the stove, and the office comes back scratchy but readable.
options.failureOutcome: Hours of tinkering and the radio stays dead, its parts spread across a tarp in an order only he understands. The town run happens anyway — a day later and a day poorer.

options.label: Work without radio — check in when you can
options.outcome: Nothing happens that needed a radio. You borrow the neighbouring crew's set twice for check-ins, and the replacement can wait for the regular supply run.
options.failureOutcome: The office has been calling for two days about a BCWS shutdown you never heard. Silence reads as dodging — a WorkSafeBC officer, tipped by the office's own check-in log, shows up with a written order about check-in procedure (OHS Reg. 4.21), and the file it starts stays open.

options.label: Stand down until comms are restored; drive to the repeater for the check-in
options.outcome: Nobody works in the bush without a check-in procedure. The crew stays in camp on maps and plot cards while the driver runs up to the repeater to check in and order the part. A day mostly lost, and nothing to explain.

title: Fuel Contamination
description: The diesel smells wrong. Water got into the fuel barrel somehow. The truck sputters and stalls.

options.label: Drain and filter what you can
options.outcome: Tedious work with a chamois and a funnel. You save about half the fuel, and the equipment runs rough for a day before clearing its throat.
options.failureOutcome: The water is through every can, not just the barrel. You save a quarter of it, the truck's injectors are already scored from the morning's running, and the fresh-fuel order goes in anyway — with a truck limping until it comes.

options.label: Dump it all and order fresh fuel
options.outcome: The safe choice but you're grounded until the delivery arrives.

options.label: Use it anyway — it's mostly diesel
options.outcome: The truck runs, barely, on what you tell yourself is mostly diesel. Something is going to break sooner rather than later.
options.failureOutcome: The injection pump seizes with the crummy halfway up the spur, and a dead truck there is a roadblock, not a breakdown. Parts are days out, and everything walks around it until they come.

title: Planting Crew Drifting Across the Line
description: Another contractor's planting crew has started on the adjacent opening and their planters are drifting across your boundary ribbon. Their foreman keeps calling it an honest mistake.

options.label: Talk to their foreman over the hood
options.outcome: A heated but productive conversation over the hood of his pickup. The boundary gets re-ribboned while you both watch. Uneasy truce.
options.failureOutcome: He is not interested in a conversation, and the shouting carries. By the weekend there is a written complaint about your crew on the licensee's desk, and their planters are ten metres further over than they were.

options.label: Report the encroachment to the office
options.outcome: Phone calls and a GPS track of the ribbon. The office sorts it out with the other contractor and the checker re-plots the line. Takes days to resolve.

options.label: Race them to the line
options.outcome: Both crews push to bury each other, and yours wins by a bag. Dangerous, loud, and the best week of morale all season.
options.failureOutcome: Racing does not leave time to look at the ribbon. Your fastest planter runs a bag through the riparian reserve and rolls an ankle on the way out. She is limping, the plots in the reserve are a stocking problem, and you lose the race anyway — their foreman makes sure the whole valley hears.

title: Urgent Call from Home
description: The sat phone rings. It's for one of your crew members — a family emergency back home. He's white-faced and shaking.

options.label: Let him go immediately
options.outcome: He drives out within the hour. The crew understands. You're short-handed but it's the right thing.

options.label: Ask him to stay until the shift ends
options.outcome: He stays and works like a machine because thinking is worse. The crew gives him room and nobody says anything to you about it. He is on the road by dark.
options.failureOutcome: His mind is on the highway and his saw is not. The kickback takes him across the thigh — the chaps eat most of it, first aid takes the rest. You drive him out that evening anyway, and the crew watches you load his gear without a word on your behalf.

options.label: Drive him to town yourself
options.outcome: You personally deliver him to the bus station. The crew respects the gesture enormously.

title: Eagle Nest in the Block
description: A bald eagle nest sits in a big veteran Douglas-fir inside the boundary you're flagging. Two chicks are visible. Nest trees are protected under the Wildlife Act whether or not anyone has mapped them.

options.label: GPS the nest tree, flag a WTP around it, note the buffer in the site plan
options.outcome: You GPS the tree, ribbon a wildlife tree patch around it, and write the buffer and the timing window into the notes for the site plan. Adds distance to the boundary and takes a few stems out of the block — and nobody has to revisit it.

options.label: Note it and let the planner decide
options.outcome: A point in the GPS and a line in the field book. The planner picks it up in the office review and the buffer goes in on the map. It worked, this time.
options.failureOutcome: The point gets lost between your field book and the site plan, and the block goes to permit with the nest tree inside the boundary. The district's wildlife biologist finds it on the pre-harvest walk instead of you. The CP waits for the amendment, and the question of who noticed and said nothing has your name on it.

options.label: Leave it off the map
options.outcome: The boundary goes where the timber is. The nest stays out of the notes, and the adults keep bringing fish to it all week while you flag past.
options.failureOutcome: The nest was never a secret — the neighbour across the valley has been watching that pair for years. The complaint goes to COS, the district walks the block with your ribbon in the photos, and an eagle nest inside a boundary you flagged is a Wildlife Act file whether or not anyone has cut a tree. The block stops for the assessment, and the file follows the licence, not the block.

title: Missing Gear
description: Two chainsaws and a fuel can are missing from camp. Either someone took them or a very talented bear has new hobbies.

options.label: Search the area thoroughly
options.outcome: You find one saw tossed in the brush a hundred metres out — dropped by somebody moving fast. The rest is gone, but one back is one back.
options.failureOutcome: Half a day of grid-walking turns up nothing of yours — then all of it, tarped and staged by the old pullout for pickup. Whoever it is, they are coming back for the load. Camp security is now the evening's plan, not sleep.

options.label: Report theft to RCMP
options.outcome: Officers visit camp. Lots of questions, no answers. The crew feels violated.

options.label: Quietly increase camp security
options.outcome: You set up watches and lock everything down. No more incidents but the crew is on edge.

title: Spring Breakup Starting
description: The frost is coming out of the ground. Roads that were solid yesterday are turning to mush. The window for getting trucks into the block is closing fast.

options.label: Push the trucks in while the frost holds — early starts, late finishes
options.outcome: You run the trucks in before dawn while the frost holds the road together and walk out after dark. Exhausting, hard on the vehicles, and worth every hour of it.
options.partialOutcome: On the second morning the crummy goes in to the frame on a stretch that held all day. Six hours of digging and matting gets it out, and that is the end of it — the road will not take a truck again until it dries.
options.failureOutcome: The loaded crummy punches through the road base where the frost went out from underneath, and it sits down to the frame. The truck is buried, the road is destroyed behind it, and the road permit holder's repair bill arrives before the tow does. Vehicle access is done for the season, and everything now comes in on foot or waits.

options.label: Walk in from the mainline — foot access only
options.outcome: Long walks, light packs, no wheels past the mainline. Slow going but no road damage.

options.label: Shut down and wait for the roads to firm up
options.outcome: The responsible choice. The trucks stay parked at the mainline. Could be a week or more.

title: Fresh Water Spring
description: A crew member finds a clear, cold spring bubbling up through the rocks. Crystal-clear water, probably safe to drink.

options.label: Fill up all the water containers
options.outcome: Fresh, cold water for the whole camp, and the coffee finally tastes like something. Everyone's in better spirits.
options.failureOutcome: A week on, three of the crew can't hold food down, and the clinic in town says giardia over the radio. First aid goes fast, production goes slow, and every drop in camp gets boiled from here to the end of the trip.

options.label: Test it first, use it if clean
options.outcome: You use purification tablets just to be safe. Smart move — the water is perfect.

options.label: Note location and stick with camp water
options.outcome: Better safe than sorry. You GPS the spring for future reference.

title: Drone Flyover Opportunity
description: A forestry tech from another operation offers to fly his drone over your block during his lunch break. He's got a mapping camera.

options.label: Accept — map the whole block
options.outcome: Incredible aerial data. You can see drainage patterns, terrain features, and optimal routes from above.

options.label: Ask him to scout the road ahead
options.outcome: The drone reveals a major washout two kilometres ahead. You reroute and save a day.

options.label: Decline — don't need outside help
options.outcome: Your choice. The crew shrugs.

title: Something in the Dark
description: Something big crashes through the brush near camp at 2 AM. Flashlight beams catch reflective eyes before it disappears. Nobody's sure what it was.

options.label: Post a watch for the rest of the night
options.outcome: Nothing else happens. The watchers are wrecked the next day, but everyone else sleeps easier.

options.label: Check tracks in the morning
options.outcome: Wolverine tracks. Impressive animal, not dangerous to the camp. Tensions ease.

options.label: Ignore it and go back to sleep
options.outcome: Whatever it was, it moved on. Some of the crew sleep fine; the rest don't close their eyes until the sky goes grey.
options.failureOutcome: It was a bear, and it found what it was smelling for. The cache is torn open at dawn — bags dragged into the brush, a cooler cracked like an egg. A fed bear comes back, and tonight's problem is now every night's problem until it is dealt with.

title: Swollen Creek Crossing
description: Recent rain has the creek running high. It's passable, maybe, but the current is strong and the bottom is uncertain.

options.label: Probe on foot, then drive across
options.outcome: You wade in waist-deep, feeling for the bottom with a peavey. Solid gravel the whole way. The trucks cross one at a time and nobody says much about how cold you are.
options.partialOutcome: Halfway across, the lead truck finds the soft spot you missed. It settles to the axle and stays there. Two hours on the winch and everything in the boxes is wet.
options.failureOutcome: The bottom is not gravel, it is rounded cobble over silt, and it moves. The truck slews downstream and takes water through the intake before you get a line on it. You are back on the near bank with a drowned engine and a creek that is still rising.

options.label: Wait for the water to drop
options.outcome: By afternoon it's lower. Safe crossing but half a day lost.

options.label: Build a temporary crossing
options.outcome: Logs, gravel, and two hours of swearing make a rough crib crossing. It holds for one truck at a time, and you leave it better than you found the ford.
options.failureOutcome: The crib shifts under the second truck and the whole works racks sideways into the current. The truck sits in the creek to the box floor, everything soft in it is soaked, and what is left of your bridge is downstream. Nobody is crossing here now.

title: An Elder Visits Camp

managerVariant.title: Culturally Modified Trees - Work Paused
managerVariant.description: An Elder from the local Nation has identified culturally modified trees inside the active block. The superintendent has paused work at the boundary and wants head office direction before another tree comes down.

options.label: Stand the block down and walk it with her
options.outcome: The stewardship forester spends a day among bark-stripped cedars with centuries of history. The cut plan changes; the relationship doesn't have to.

options.label: Log the concern and keep the block moving
options.outcome: The file notes it. She notices what the file is for.

options.label: Retain her as a cultural monitor for the division
options.outcome: An added line in the budget and a standing seat at the table. The certification auditor and the Nation both approve.

description: An Elder from the Nation arrives at camp. She says there are culturally modified trees nearby that need protection. She's calm but serious.

options.label: Stop work and walk the area with her
options.outcome: She shows you bark-stripped cedars with centuries of history. You move the boundary together and flag the CMTs for the site plan.

options.label: Acknowledge and promise to investigate later
options.outcome: She's skeptical but accepts your word, and nothing the crew ribbons this week proves her right. The relationship is strained, and you still owe the walk.
options.failureOutcome: Wednesday the compassman runs line straight through a stand of bark-stripped cedars nobody flagged, because nobody looked, and blazes two of them for the boundary. A fresh blaze in a CMT is a Heritage Conservation Act problem, not a misunderstanding. The office pulls the crew off the block, the Archaeology Branch opens a file, and the Elder does not come back to talk.

options.label: Offer to hire her as a cultural monitor
options.outcome: She agrees. An added cost but the relationship and compliance benefits are enormous.

title: Natural Mineral Lick
description: You find a natural mineral lick heavily used by wildlife. Dozens of tracks — deer, elk, moose, bear — converge on this muddy depression.

options.label: Flag it and establish a buffer
options.outcome: The right thing to do. The planner and the district's wildlife biologist will want the point, and the buffer goes in the site plan.

options.label: Route around it quietly
options.outcome: You adjust the plan without formally reporting. Saves paperwork.

options.label: Set up a trail camera for fun
options.outcome: The crew checks the camera every morning like kids on Christmas. Incredible footage.

title: Hydraulic Line Burst
description: The site-prep excavator's hydraulic line ruptures, spraying hot fluid everywhere. The machine drops its bucket and goes dead. There's oil soaking into the ground.

options.label: Contain the spill immediately
options.outcome: You deploy absorbent pads, dig a containment trench, and call the spill in. Machine is down but the spill is managed.

options.label: Try to patch the line in the field
options.outcome: Hose clamps and a length of spare line. It holds at reduced pressure and the excavator finishes the shift, slowly, with somebody watching the coupling the whole time.
options.partialOutcome: The patch holds until the middle of the next shift, then lets go again in a worse place. You end up making the mechanic call you were trying to avoid, and cleaning up a second spill to go with the first.
options.failureOutcome: The clamp lets go while the line is still charged and catches the man working next to it across the forearm. Hot fluid at pressure does not care about a glove. The machine is down anyway and now so is he.

options.label: Shut everything down and call for a mechanic
options.outcome: The contractor's mechanic takes two days. Expensive but done right. You report the spill to the provincial spill line and log the cleanup.

title: Perfect Planting Conditions
description: Cool air, overcast, soft ground, no wind. Every planter is hitting numbers and the checker can't find a fault. The crew is in a groove.

options.label: Ride the momentum — keep pushing
options.outcome: An exceptional day. The crew celebrates with extra rations at dinner.

options.label: Bank the good day and quit early
options.outcome: Ahead of schedule, so you call it at 3 PM. Rest and recovery.

title: Dense Morning Fog
description: You can't see twenty metres. The forest has vanished into white. Running line in this is asking for trouble — you can't see the danger trees, let alone the ribbon.

options.label: Wait for it to burn off
options.outcome: By 10 AM the sun wins. Late start but safe.

options.label: Do truck work until it clears
options.outcome: Plot cards, GPS downloads, ribbon inventory — no line work. Decent use of time.

options.label: Run line anyway, tight spacing, voice contact
options.outcome: Slow, tense work — every call answered, every danger tree called by voice. One close call that makes everyone sweat, but the line keeps moving.
options.failureOutcome: A dead fir lets go in the white and comes down where the compassman was not. It misses him and finds the quad. Line work is done for the day, and the crew makes it plain they will not run line in fog again this trip.

title: Supply Delivery Arrives Early
description: The supply truck shows up two days early. The driver says he had a cancellation and thought he'd swing by.

options.label: Full resupply — load up on everything
options.outcome: Fuel, food, parts — you take it all. Full stocks feel great.

options.label: Just grab what you're low on
options.outcome: A targeted resupply. Smart spending.

options.label: Send out your sick/injured crew member
options.outcome: The truck can take someone to town for proper medical care. Good opportunity.

title: Old Ribbon Doesn't Match the Map
description: The old flagging peters out and the last tie point doesn't sit where the map says it should. If the boundary goes in wrong, the block ends up somewhere it isn't permitted to be.

options.label: Tie into the last known point and re-run the line
options.outcome: You walk back to the last pin you trust, shoot it in, and re-run the line from there with the GPS and a compass. Takes the rest of the day but the boundary is right, and the notes say why.

options.label: Trust the old ribbon and keep flagging
options.outcome: You follow the faded tape and back yourself. When the office overlays the track weeks later you were inside a few metres the whole way. Nobody ever finds out you guessed.
options.partialOutcome: You are off, but you are off on your own side. The block edge wanders where it should run straight, and the shape of it is going to be somebody's question at the next audit.
options.failureOutcome: You were very wrong. When the block is logged next winter the line you followed puts the harvest crew forty metres into the neighbouring licence, and the stumps do not move. Stop-work goes on the block, C&E opens a trespass file, and the ribbon in the photos is yours.

options.label: Call the office for the survey plan
options.outcome: They dig up the survey plan and the original tie notes and talk you through it over the radio. Accurate but slow.

title: Apprentice Makes a Bad Cut
description: Your newest crew member on the spacing saw drops a stem the wrong way. It hangs up in a leave tree — a dangerous 'widow maker' situation. He looks terrified.

options.label: Talk him through fixing it safely
options.outcome: You stand at his shoulder and talk him through it — escape route first, then the wedges, then the cut. The stem comes down clean and he stands a little taller after. Takes an hour.
options.failureOutcome: Halfway through the lesson the hung stem lets go on its own schedule. It grazes his shoulder going down — a bruise and a torn sleeve, pure luck at that. He hands you the saw, done with saw work for the trip, and the crew is asking quietly why the kid was under it at all.

options.label: Fix it yourself and send him to the truck
options.outcome: You handle it quickly but he's humiliated. Other crew members snicker.

options.label: Pull it down with the truck's winch
options.outcome: Brute force solution. Works but burns fuel and is hard on the winch.

title: Forgotten Tool Cache
description: Under a deadfall, someone spots a weathered toolbox and a rolled-up tarp. Previous crew must have stashed them and forgot to come back.

options.label: Claim the tools for your crew
options.outcome: A spare chain, two files, a peavey, and some wedges. The tarp is still waterproof. Great find.
options.failureOutcome: Three days on, a trapper walks into camp with your tire tracks memorized. The gear goes back plus a case of food to settle it, and his account of company crews travels the valley ahead of you.

options.label: Try to find the original owner
options.outcome: You track down a grateful survey crew from the next valley. The tools go home; the goodwill stays.
options.failureOutcome: Two camps and a radio relay later, nobody claims it. The toolbox rides in the truck bed, still not yours, and the day is spent.

options.label: Leave it — could be someone's active cache
options.outcome: You mark the spot and leave everything. Respectful, if a bit wasteful.

title: Breakfast Stories
description: Over breakfast, someone starts telling stories from past jobs. One by one, the whole crew joins in. Laughter carries across camp before the shift begins.

options.label: Join in and share your own story
options.outcome: You tell the one about the time you got lost for three days. Everyone howls. The crew starts the shift in good spirits.

options.label: Listen and let the crew bond
options.outcome: Sometimes the boss just needs to shut up and listen. The crew appreciates it.

options.label: Remind everyone the shift is starting
options.outcome: The mood deflates instantly. Professional but joyless.

title: Eco-tourism Opportunity
description: With the grove reserved, a local outfitter wants to build a guided walk to it — and wants the company's name on the boardwalk.

options.label: Back the eco-tourism pitch ($1,500)
options.outcome: You front the guiding outfit's first season. By fall, the boardwalk to the grove has a guestbook with three hundred names in it — several of them district staff.
options.failureOutcome: The outfit folds before Labour Day — two cancelled bookings and a van that was never paid for. The boardwalk grays half-built, and every coffee-row skeptic in the district now has their example of what protection pays.

options.label: Decline politely
options.outcome: You pass. The grove stays standing and protected on paper; the opportunity drives off in someone else's truck.

title: Blockade on the Spur
description: The diameters got out. Activists have blockaded the spur road below the grove, demanding it be pulled from the block before the CP is issued.

options.label: Negotiate and offer partial protection
options.outcome: Two tense days at the blockade end with a map on a tailgate: the oldest stand comes out of the block, the rest stays in. Nobody is happy, which the mediator calls success.
options.partialOutcome: The moderates sign the tailgate map; the hardliners walk into the trees without a word. Within the week there are fresh spikes chalked on the spur and someone glassing the block from the ridge.
options.failureOutcome: Two days of talk end with the mediator packing up mid-sentence. The blockade is wider than it was Monday, a camera crew is due Thursday, and clearing it or conceding the grove are both uglier choices now.

options.label: Get an injunction and ask the RCMP to enforce it
options.outcome: The RCMP clear the road by noon. The footage clears the evening news by six. Legal fees and a cold district office follow.
options.failureOutcome: An officer drags a grey-haired birdwatcher across the cattle guard on camera and the clip runs nationally by morning. A judge signs an interim injunction before the weekend — the grove is off-limits until the hearing, and your name is in the affidavit.

title: Hauler Short on Grub
description: A logging truck idles at the pullout. The hauler leans out: three days from town, cook shack burned through its stores, and he is offering diesel for anything resembling dinner.

options.label: Trade 10 food for a jerry transfer
options.outcome: You pump 15 fuel off his saddle tank while he loads a rations box. Both crews leave happier.

options.label: Give him a meal, no charge
options.outcome: He eats, waves, and radios your good name up the road. Word travels on these frequencies.

options.label: Keep your stores
options.outcome: He shrugs and grinds off. You keep your food and your anonymity.

title: Survey Crew Wants Your Chains
description: A timber cruising crew flags you down. They are headed up the pass with bald tires and money, and they can see the tire chains lashed to your rack.

options.label: Sell the spare chains ($260)
options.outcome: Cash changes hands. You hope the weather holds for you lower down.

options.label: Swap chains for their first aid stock
options.outcome: They carry doubles of everything. Two sealed kits for the chains — a trade both sides brag about.

options.label: Not for sale
options.outcome: They wish you luck with the tone of people who will need it more than you.

title: Camp Cook's Surplus
description: A silviculture camp is demobilizing early. Their cook has a wall of untouched food boxes and instructions not to haul them back over the pass.

options.label: Buy the lot cheap ($90)
options.outcome: Twenty-five food for less than town prices. The cook throws in a bag of real coffee.

options.label: Trade a field repair for food
options.outcome: Your mechanic tunes their generator; the cook loads your truck. Fair is fair.

options.label: Pass
options.outcome: The boxes go to the gray jays. A crime, your crew mutters.

title: The Trapper's Price
description: An old trapper watches you glass the next drainage from his cabin step. He knows every crossing and washout ahead — and he knows what that knowledge is worth.

options.label: Trade 8 food for the lay of the land
options.outcome: He draws the drainage in the dust: which crossing is honest, which road is a lie. Gold.

options.label: Buy his route notes ($150)
options.outcome: Pages of tight pencil from thirty winters. Your traverse plan just got smarter.

options.label: Decline politely
options.outcome: He nods like he has seen your kind before. He has.

title: Grader Operator's Offer
description: A road grader is parked at the junction, operator eating lunch. For fuel or cash he could blade the worst kilometre of the spur you are dreading.

options.label: Pay for the blade work ($200)
options.outcome: Thirty minutes of grader beats a day of winching. The spur rides smooth.

options.label: Trade 12 fuel for the pass
options.outcome: He tops up, you roll through behind the blade. Handshake economics.

options.label: Take the spur as it lies
options.outcome: Your suspension files a grievance. The crew co-signs it.
options.failureOutcome: The dreaded kilometre is worse than advertised. The lead truck drops to the frame in a rut and a leaf spring lets go coming out; half a day on the winch and you make camp late with the toolbox open.

title: Monitors Heading In
description: Two Guardians from the local Nation are heading into the same country for water sampling. Their truck is heavy on gear and light on fuel; yours is the opposite.

options.label: Split fuel, share the road in
options.outcome: You convoy in together, trading fuel for their read on the creeks. Their water knowledge is better than your maps.

options.label: Offer fuel, ask nothing
options.outcome: They wave it off twice, take it once, and remember it longer than you will.

options.label: Tight nod, keep rolling
options.outcome: Nothing lost. Nothing built, either.

title: Planter Bus at the Fork
description: A crummy full of tree planters is stopped at the fork, out of motion-sickness bags and nearly out of snacks. Their foreman holds up a first aid kit like a white flag.

options.label: Trade 6 food for the kit
options.outcome: Granola bars go one way, a sealed kit comes the other. The bus erupts in weak cheering.

options.label: Sell snacks at bush prices ($80)
options.outcome: Capitalism finds a way, even at a gravel fork. The foreman pays without blinking.

options.label: Wave and drive on
options.outcome: In the mirror, forty hungry faces watch you go.

title: Outfitter's Barter
description: A hunting outfitter's wall tent camp sits above the creek. He has smoked meat, spare lantern fuel, and a broken generator he would dearly love running before clients fly in.

options.label: Fix his generator for meat and fuel
options.outcome: An hour of wrenching buys smoked moose and ten litres of fuel. Everyone at the fire agrees this is the correct economy.
options.failureOutcome: You pull the cover and the smell tells you first — windings, fried, no field fix. The hour is gone, the payment was contingent, and his clients fly into a dark camp with your name attached to the story.

options.label: Buy smoked meat ($120)
options.outcome: Expensive, and worth it. Camp dinner becomes an event.

options.label: Keep moving
options.outcome: The smell of the smoker follows the truck for a kilometre. The crew suffers audibly.
